cards.text: This one's short, friend: thirteen verses, and I've read cookie recipes longer than that! A man who calls himself the elder is writing to the chosen lady and her children. He tells them he loves them, and he's not the only one.

cards.question: The elder says he and others love the chosen lady and her children because of the ___ that abides in us.
Next, the elder blesses them with grace, mercy and peace. Along with God the Father, who does he say these come from?

answers.text: Jesus Christ the Son of the Father
The apostles who walked with Him
The angels who serve before Him

cards.text: Now the elder has news about some of the lady's children, and it makes him OVERJOYED. Not joyed. OVERjoyed. That's my face when a whole batch comes out and NOTHING is burnt!

cards.question: What did the elder find some of the chosen lady's children doing that made him so happy?

cards.text: Then the elder turns to the dear lady and urges her to keep a commandment.

cards.question: Which commandment does the elder urge the dear lady to keep?

answers.text: That we rest on the Sabbath

cards.question: The elder calls the commandment to love one another a brand new commandment.

cards.text: So what IS love? The elder's about to spell it out, and I'm leaning in like it's the last thirty seconds on the oven timer.

cards.question: The elder says love means walking according to His commandments.

cards.text: Then he adds that the commandment they've heard from the beginning is to walk in love. Love is walking in His commandments, and the commandment is to walk in love, round and round like dough in my mixer!
Then the elder's tone changes, friend. He says many deceivers have gone out into the world.

cards.question: What do the deceivers the elder warns about refuse to confess?

answers.text: The coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh
The creation of the heavens and earth
The words of the prophets of old

cards.question: The elder says anyone who refuses to confess this is the deceiver and the ___.

cards.text: So the elder gives them a warning: watch yourselves. When a man who's OVERJOYED a minute ago says that, you listen!

cards.question: Why does the elder tell the chosen lady and her children to watch themselves?

answers.text: So they won't lose what we've worked for
So the deceivers won't find their house
So no one can accuse them falsely

cards.text: Then the elder talks about anyone who runs ahead without remaining in the teaching of Christ. He says that person does not have God.

cards.question: The elder says whoever remains in the teaching of Christ has the Father but not the Son.

cards.text: Now he gets practical. What should they do when someone shows up at the door without this teaching?

cards.question: If someone comes to the chosen lady without the teaching of Christ, what does the elder tell her to do?

answers.text: Not welcome him in or even greet him
Give him a bed for one night only
Bring him before the church to be tested

cards.question: The elder says anyone who greets a person like that shares in his evil deeds.

cards.text: The elder has many more things to write, but he'd rather not use paper and ink. Friend, I spent YEARS buried under paper in the back of that drawer, so I am WITH this man!

cards.question: Instead of writing more with paper and ink, what does the elder hope to do?

answers.text: Come and speak with them face to face
Send a messenger with a longer letter
Meet them at the next feast in Jerusalem

cards.question: The elder hopes to visit so that their ___ may be complete.
At the very end of the letter, who sends greetings to the chosen lady?

answers.text: The children of her elect sister
The elders of the church in Ephesus
The brothers who are with Paul

findings.problem: Card 1 drops 'in the truth' and 'all who know the truth' from verse 1, so nothing before this blank points to 'truth' over 'joy' or 'faith'. The baker can only guess the wording of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Verse 3 doesn't say the elder blesses them. It states that grace, mercy and peace 'will be with us in truth and love'. The question also changes 'us' to 'them'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Now the elder has news…', 'Not joyed.', 'OVERjoyed.' and 'That's my face…'. A story card that isn't the opening card can have no more than two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card tells nothing from verse 6. It only teases that the elder is about to define love, yet it cites 2 John 1:6.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'Round and round like dough in my mixer' makes verse 6 sound like it is going in circles. The joke's target is the wording of Scripture itself.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 5 multiple choice cards, 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'Anyone who refuses to confess this' points back to the previous card's answer, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'A person like that' points back to card 9, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who that person is: someone who comes without the teaching of Christ.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 11 and the question both say the elder would rather not write with paper and ink. That rules out the wrong answer 'Send a messenger with a longer letter'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Verse 12 says 'so that our joy may be complete', which includes the elder. Changing it to 'their joy' leaves him out.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
